themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Surge
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints spiked to 23 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 4.8 per week, a 384% increase (z-score: 8.01), suggesting a sudden operational or enforcement shift affecting Sunnyside/Woodside residents' street access and safety.
evidence: 23 for-hire vehicle complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (384% spike, z-score: 8.01)
Complaint volume represents most acute spike on district radar besides outdoor dining and tree complaints
No prior news coverage or community board agenda items explaining the sudden surge
reporting_angles: Interview residents about congestion and illegal parking by Uber/Lyft drivers; investigate if a major rideshare hub or demand event triggered the spike
Contact TLC and rideshare companies to determine if driver behavior, app routing, or enforcement action changed this week

themes_detail.label: Unleashed Dogs in Parks
themes_detail.summary: Unleashed dog complaints jumped to 5 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 0.6 per week, a 700% increase (z-score: 6.29), indicating a potential safety and park-use conflict emerging in real time in Sunnyside/Woodside.
evidence: 5 unleashed dog complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% increase, z-score: 6.29)
Parallels spike in park noise complaints (6 last week, 700% above baseline), suggesting parks are becoming flashpoints
Community board budget request for new/expanded park amenities suggests parks are underfunded and potentially understaffed for enforcement
reporting_angles: Interview park users and dog owners to understand why enforcement appears to have broken down this week
Check with Parks Department on staffing levels and whether a park enforcement officer has left or been reassigned

themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining Complaints Explode
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints surged to 6 LAST WEEK from a 0.2 weekly baseline, a 2300% spike (z-score: 13.28), the highest statistical anomaly in the district and likely tied to seasonal restaurant expansion or sidewalk obstruction.
evidence: 6 outdoor dining complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2300% spike, z-score: 13.28—highest on district radar)
Spike corresponds with warming weather and likely post-winter restaurant reopening of sidewalk seating
Complaint type was virtually dormant before; sudden emergence suggests new or aggressive expansion by restaurants or inadequate enforcement
reporting_angles: Survey restaurants on Steinway St, Queens Blvd, and other commercial strips to determine if there's been a coordinated push to expand outdoor seating
Interview community members about what specific problems triggered complaints (sidewalk obstruction, noise, rat activity, etc.) to understand if this is quality-of-life or public space issue

themes_detail.label: Dead and Dying Trees
themes_detail.summary: Dead and dying tree complaints spiked to 4 LAST WEEK from a 0.1 weekly baseline, a 3100% increase (z-score: 11.72), suggesting either a recent storm damage event or sudden uptick in resident awareness of tree maintenance gaps.
evidence: 4 dead/dying tree complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (3100% increase, z-score: 11.72)
Second-highest statistical anomaly in district; clustering suggests geographic or event-driven cause rather than random complaints
Community board has standing budget request for park and amenity improvements, indicating prior concern about green space
reporting_angles: Check NYC Parks tree inventory database for recent storm damage, disease outbreak, or neglected maintenance in specific blocks
Interview residents to determine if complaints are clustered (e.g., one street) and whether a specific tree removal or die-off triggered community concern

themes_detail.label: Park Noise and Litter Surge
themes_detail.summary: Park noise complaints jumped to 6 LAST WEEK from a 0.8 weekly baseline (700% spike, z-score: 7.94) and litter basket requests hit 5 (1900% spike, z-score: 7.18), together painting a picture of parks becoming overcrowded, poorly maintained, or hosting disruptive activity.
evidence: Park noise: 6 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average (700% increase, z-score: 7.94)
Litter basket requests: 5 LAST WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (1900% increase, z-score: 7.18)
Two converging signals suggest parks are experiencing simultaneous overcrowding and under-maintenance; community board repeatedly requests expanded park amenities
reporting_angles: Identify which parks are generating most complaints (Sunnyside Park, Gantry Park, etc.) and document what activities or crowds are driving noise
Interview Parks Department about staffing, trash collection frequency, and why litter basket requests spiked—are existing bins full or insufficient?
